# WO-2026-08-11-01 — A numbered answer lands on the question Warwick was actually looking at

## AMENDMENT 1 — Larry, 2026-08-10, answering Keel's read-back CLARIFY

> **Attribution note.** Warwick authorised the outcome ("fix cross-shop answer routing properly").
> Everything in this amendment is **Larry's** engineering ruling on how, taken on Keel's evidence.
> None of it is a Warwick decision and none of it may be reported as one.

Keel returned **CLARIFY** at the gate and was right on every point. The order was accurate about the
machine but **too narrow about the defect** and **self-contradictory about the refusal**. What
changed, and why:

1. **The defect is four holes, not one.** Keel established, before writing anything, that the
   ordinal collision (`:464`) is the *least* dangerous of them. Step 1 (exact candidate) and step 3
   (Terra, via a `question_key` that carries no shop component) leak the same way. **Step 2 is worse
   than the one I sent it after**: it needs no number at all, so there is nothing in the message for
   a reviewer to blame afterwards. AC5 is re-cut from "establish whether" to "close all of them".
2. **`recordedAnswerMatches` has it too** and no AC covered it. Now AC5b.
3. **AC3 asked for two incompatible things** — the `outcome` promised Warwick is told, AC3 permitted
   a log line and forbade a new card. Resolved in Keel's favour and by Keel's design: re-scope the
   existing AC8 guard so the **already-shipped** `reply_not_taken` card becomes reachable in the case
   that matters (AC5c). No new surface, and the contradiction dissolves rather than needing a ruling.
4. **"Nothing is written" is now defined** as "no answer row against any question" (AC3). Intake's
   downstream behaviour is unchanged and out of scope.
5. **Strict refusal rejected, targeted scoping adopted** (AC5a) — Keel's recommendation, and better
   than my order. Strict would have deleted capability that works correctly today.

**Also acknowledged, no change required:**

- The `productionWiring.test.js:562-580` pin is a source-**text** `indexOf`, so a comment containing
  `pollIntake` near the `loadOpenQuestions` call would redden it while the wiring is correct. Keep
  comments clear of both tokens. **A red there is not automatically a real regression.**
- Every surface file is CRLF and there is no `.gitattributes`, so AC6's "prove the source changed"
  is live rather than theoretical. Hash-and-length before/after, restore in a `finally`, preserve
  CRLF on write.
- `runPipeline.test.js:1909` calls `loadOpenQuestions` directly and is outside the surface. Do not
  edit it. If a signature change would break it, that is a design signal — prefer scoping at the
  call site over changing the function's contract.
- Keel declined to verify live shop state under `credential_scope: none`. **Correct.** The live state
  is Larry's evidence, not the worker's, and the fix must hold with M64 active regardless.

## The defect, established by execution before this order was written

`loadOpenQuestions` (`pipeline/runtime.js:212`) loops the shops returned by `store.listActiveShops`
(`status NOT IN ('RECONCILED','CANCELLED')`, plus terminal shops still holding a pending consumable
command) and pushes every open question into ONE flat array, assigning `ordinal: i + 1` computed
**per shop** (`runtime.js:241`).

`correlateTypedAnswer` (`runtime.js:447`) then does, at `runtime.js:464`:

```js
const byOrdinal = new Map(open.map((q) => [q.ordinal, q]));
```

`new Map` is last-write-wins and `open` is ordered `by id ASC`. **Two active shops both produce
ordinals 1, 2, 3 — so one shop's question silently shadows the other's.** The surviving mapping
carries its own `shopRef`, which travels verbatim through `telegramAdapter.js:217-221` into
`commands.answerQuestion`, which resolves the shop by that ref and writes the answer to the WRONG
shop's row. It succeeds. It logs `board_reply_correlated`. Nothing errors, and Warwick sees nothing.

**Measured live state, read-only, this session:** shop 14 `SHOP-2026-08-10-M64` is `NEEDS_DECISION`
with open questions at board positions **1 and 3** of 8 rows. Shop 7 `SHOP-2026-08-09` is
`READY_TO_SHOP` with all 3 answered. The moment a new shop opens its own question 1, this is live.

**The board is already per-shop and it is correct.** `boardStateOf` (`runtime.js:1194`) is called
only from `queueBoard(deps, shop, …)` (`runtime.js:1316`) over `store.listQuestions(deps, shop.id)`
— one board per shop, numbered 1..N across all rows including answered ones so a number never moves
for the life of the shop. **Do not change the numbering Warwick reads.** The per-shop ordinal is not
the defect; the unscoped lookup is.

**The binding you need already exists and is not used for this.** `loadBoardTargets`
(`runtime.js:337`) and `boardAt` (`runtime.js:376`) already resolve an inbound `(chatId, messageId)`
reply to exactly one shop's board. Today that is consumed only for the AC8 "reply not taken" notice
(`runtime.js:1879`) and is never handed to `correlateTypedAnswer`.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — A numbered reply is scoped to the board it answers.** When the inbound message is a reply to
a known question board, the ordinal lookup resolves against **that shop's questions only**. A
question belonging to any other shop is not a candidate, whatever its number.

**AC2 — Two simultaneously active shops, proven in BOTH directions.** *(AMENDMENT 1 adds AC2b below;
this clause is unchanged.)* With shops A and B both active
and each holding an open question numbered N: a reply `"N: <text>"` on A's board answers A's
question N **and leaves B's question N `open` with a null answer**; and the mirrored case answers B
and leaves A open. Two separate assertions. A test that passes only because the higher shop id
happens to win is not evidence — assert the untouched shop explicitly, by status and answer value.

**AC3 — Ambiguity is refused, never guessed, and never silent.** *(RE-CUT by AMENDMENT 1 — the
original wording was self-contradictory and is superseded, not appended to.)*

When a mapping cannot be bound to exactly one shop, **no answer row is recorded against any
question.** That is what "nothing is written" means here — intake's own downstream behaviour is
unchanged and out of scope; a list row appearing by that route is not a violation of this AC.

The refusal emits a distinct log event **and** Warwick is told through the **existing**
`reply_not_taken` outbox card. Do not invent a new card. See AC5c for the guard change that makes
that card reachable in the case that matters.

**AC2b — The three non-ordinal holes are each proven closed, by their own test.** *(AMENDMENT 1.)*
One test per hole, each RED against the unmodified source:

- **exact-candidate (`runtime.js:482`)** — one label offered by a question in each of two shops; a
  reply must not be written to the shop he was not addressing.
- **single-open-question (`runtime.js:497`) — the worst one, and it carries no number at all.**
  Shop A's board fully answered, shop B holds one open question, Warwick replies to A's board. Today
  B's question is answered with words aimed at A. Assert B is untouched and that Warwick receives the
  `reply_not_taken` card.
- **Terra `byKey` (`runtime.js:537`)** — two active shops asking about the SAME item name therefore
  minting the identical `question_key`. Assert the answer lands on the shop whose board was replied
  to, and that the other shop's identically-keyed row is untouched.

**AC4 — The single-shop journey is unchanged in substance.** With exactly one active shop holding
open questions, every existing behaviour is preserved: bare typed answers, one reply answering
several numbered questions, exact-candidate matching, the single-open-question path, and the Terra
step. `runtime.test.js:2338` must still pass unmodified in substance.

**AC5 — Close the other three correlation steps too.** *(RE-CUT by AMENDMENT 1. The original asked
you to "establish whether" they leak. You established that all three do, before implementing, which
is what the gate is for. They are now IN SCOPE and the requirement is TARGETED, not strict.)*

**AC5a — Targeted scoping, not strict refusal.** Where the inbound message IS a reply to a resolvable
board, scope the candidate set to that board's shop **once, before correlation begins**, so all four
steps inherit one scope from one place. Where there is NO board to bind to, do not disable
correlation — instead drop any mapping whose key or label is offered by **more than one shop**, and
keep it where it is unique across the whole open set. This is already this function's own declared
doctrine at `runtime.js:428-431` ("Two questions offering the SAME label is ambiguous, so it falls
through to the model rather than picking the first"); you are extending it across shops, not
inventing a rule. **Strict refusal is explicitly rejected** — it would delete the exact-candidate and
Terra paths that work correctly today.

**AC5b — `recordedAnswerMatches` (`runtime.js:277`) is IN SCOPE.** Its `open.find(q => q.questionKey
=== questionKey)` spans shops and is on the live `cardRow` branch at `:1823`. Same defect class, same
fix, inside your surface. Leaving it while fixing its three siblings would be a half-closed defect
class, which is the failure this order exists to end.

**AC5c — The AC8 guard at `runtime.js:1879` becomes per-board-shop.** It currently fires only when
`openQuestions.length === 0` **globally**, which is why your step-2 case is invisible: shop A's board
is fully answered, shop B has one open, Warwick replies to A, and B's question is answered with words
aimed at A — with no number anywhere to blame. Change the condition to *"the shop whose board he
replied to has nothing open"*. With exactly one active shop the two conditions are identical, so AC4
is untouched. **This is the change that makes AC3's "Warwick is told" true through a card that
already exists.**

**AC5d — Do NOT change `questionKeyFor`.** You correctly found that `keys.js:260-274` derives the key
from the item name with no shop component, so two shops asking about the same item collide by key.
That derivation is **data-shaped and pinned byte-for-byte** (`keys.js:253-258` — three live shops
carry rows keyed by it). Scope the **lookup**, never the key. Changing it is a REFUSE condition.

**AC6 — Mutation proof, both directions, with the source proven to have changed.** For AC1 and AC3
separately: mutate the delivered guard, prove the new test goes RED, restore, prove GREEN. **Assert
the source file actually changed before believing any red** — a CRLF no-op silently produces a false
green here and has done so four times on this estate. Report the executed test count for every run;
`0 executed` is a FAILURE, never a pass. Restore in a `finally`, or mutate a copy.

**AC7 — No new mechanism.** No registry, no ordinal service, no new table, no schema change, no new
runtime dependency. If the fix appears to need one, that is a finding to report, not to build.
